newsitem.title: UK: Nigerian spot premiums ride higher with gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian spot premiums ride higher with gas oil.

text.p: Nigerian spot crude differentials took off on Wednesday as dealers competed to grab cargoes of the West African producer's gas oil-rich grades for November loading.
"The market is really taking off, but everything's being kept under wraps," said one trader.
Dealers said cargoes of Forcados had traded at a 20-cent premium over official selling prices, due to be released next week.
They said Dated Brent-related differentials for Forcados were difficult to pin down, with trades kept private ahead of Nigerian National Petroleum Corp's pricing announcement.
But Forcados buyers had appeared in the low 70 cent premiums over Brent, they said.
Bonny Light and Qua Iboe, lighter crudes but with less gas oil than Forcados, were mostly sold out for November with a number of private trades at Dated Brent +65-70 cents.
In the Mediterranean, sour Urals appeared to have bottomed out in a trade at Dated Brent -75 cents c+f Augusta on Tuesday.
"I can't see it falling to an 80-cent discount because refining margins are so good," said a trader.
Premium Algerian grades were valued below term contract prices at discounts of around 10 cents for Saharan Blend and Zarzaitine.
North Sea physical markets were quietly firm with little crude remaining for October.
One of the Oct 24-26 Brent cargoes passing through the chains today was kept by Murphy, the equity holder, and was not for resale in the market, traders said.
